title: Route Parameters and Query Parameters
summary: Read path parameters for resource identity and query parameters for optional filtering.

sketchBlocks.title: Route parameters let one handler serve many resource ids

tryItExercises.title: Look up a club by route id
tryItExercises.prompt: Implement `GET /api/clubs/:id`. Convert the route id to a number, find the matching club, return `404` JSON when absent, otherwise return the club with `200`.
tryItExercises.hint: The path value begins as text, while the provided object ids are numbers.

help.concept: A route parameter supplies resource identity; the handler converts, looks up, and handles the missing-resource branch.
help.hint_1: Read the value from the route-parameter object on the request.
help.hint_2: Return from the 404 branch so the success response does not also run.

sourceChecks.message: Convert the route id to a number.
Find a club from the collection.
Return a 404 JSON response for a missing club.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Read optional filters from the query string
sketchBlocks.title: Query parameters refine a collection without changing its identity

tryItExercises.title: Filter events by category
tryItExercises.prompt: Implement `GET /api/events`. Read optional `req.query.category`; when it exists, return only matching events. Without the query value, return the full collection.
tryItExercises.hint: Choose a result array; do not remove items from the original `events` collection.

help.concept: Query parameters provide optional collection filters while the collection route remains the same.
help.hint_1: Read the value from `req.query` before deciding which array to return.
help.hint_2: Use a non-mutating array operation for the filtered branch.

sourceChecks.message: Filter the event collection without mutation.
Return the selected result as JSON.

quizDraft.title: Choose the identity parameter
quizDraft.prompt: Which request value should identify the required event id in `GET /api/events/:id`?
quizDraft.hint: The id is part of the matched path rather than an optional collection filter.

help.concept: Route parameters represent variable path segments used for resource identity.
help.hint_1: Look for the request property associated with named path segments.
help.hint_2: Query values belong after `?` and are better suited to optional controls.

quizDraft.title: Match parameters to their jobs
quizDraft.prompt: Which two statements describe the parameter conventions taught here?
quizDraft.hint: One parameter form is required by the resource path; the other optionally refines a collection.

help.concept: Route and query parameters carry different kinds of request information.
help.hint_1: Resource identity belongs in the path pattern.
help.hint_2: Optional filtering can leave the collection path unchanged.

options: A route parameter can identify one required resource id.
A query parameter can optionally filter a collection.
A query parameter must always be present for every GET route.
A route parameter is used only to choose the server port.

quizDraft.title: Complete the missing-resource contract
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the status code that represents a requested resource that does not exist.
quizDraft.hint: Use the client-facing status for a resource path that was valid but had no matching resource.

help.concept: A missing resource in a valid lookup route is represented with the not-found HTTP status.
help.hint_1: It is not a success status.
help.hint_2: It also does not mean the server crashed.

quizDraft.template: When `GET /api/events/:id` cannot find the requested event, the route returns status [blank1].

quizDraft.title: Order a resource lookup
quizDraft.hint: The collection cannot be searched correctly until the incoming id has the expected type.

help.concept: Resource lookup follows parameter extraction, normalization, lookup, then response branching.
help.hint_1: Start with the incoming path value.
help.hint_2: The response decision comes after lookup succeeds or fails.

tokens: Convert it to the data's id type
correctOrder: Convert it to the data's id type
